system.summary: Gronsfeld-type shift over the 27-letter Spanish alphabet (A-N, Ñ, O-Z) with the key 313 (cipher = plain +3, +1, +3, repeating), the cycle starting at the first letter of each run and running on through it; spaces dropped inside a run; runs typed in capitals inside clear Spanish.
system.notes: Key published by Narváez (2015, 2019) for the Wellington letter DCXXI.6.588.1, applied unchanged. Typing slips: single wrong letters, N typed without its bar for Ñ, and runs where the cycle is lost.

prior_solution.where: Later-hand pencil and ink glosses over about ten runs of DCXXI.6.576.1 pp. 1-2 and a handwritten slip (.0001) give the clear of a few runs (compared after decoding, not used). Narváez (2015 pp. 123-127; 2019 pp. 364-369) discusses only the Wellington letter DCXXI.6.588.1 (the parent); neither letter is named or read in print as far as checked. CEHM catalogue 91616: 'incluye clave sin descifrar'.

conditions.human_role: Set as a task for AI agents on behalf of Andrew Beling, who decided on 25 Nov 2026 that the CEHM-Carso images may be used with AI readers (plan frozen before decoding, blind second transcription, strict counting); AI agents transcribed, decoded, read, counted and translated. No person checked the text.
tools: scripts in this folder (decryption, trigram and word-coverage test against random keys, word count)
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), viewing the images; a second instance for the blind transcription

solution.what: 24 page images of six letters fetched from visor.cehm.org.mx (plain http, one at a time, no login); DCXXI.6.576.1.0009 does not exist (404).
Every capital-letter run of six letters transcribed twice by separate AI agents, the second blind; both hashed before decoding; differences settled on the image.

Plan frozen before decoding (PLAN.md, SHA-256 304a1ffa...): Narváez's key 313 unchanged on six letters; Spanish trigram score against 1,000 random shift triples and rank among all 19,683; word coverage at least 0.50 and above 100 random triples. DCXXI.6.576.1 and DCXXI.8.731.1 pass (rank 1 of 19,683; coverage 0.708 and 0.645 against control maxima 0.075 and 0.118). DCXXI.5.442.1 misses on coverage (0.383; trigram rank 1); DCXXI.6.624.1, 7.647.1 and 7.657.2 miss (number-letter groups, another system).

Decoder checks: Narváez's printed paragraph of the Wellington letter reproduced for two runs; the other two only up to cycle slips he restarts by hand (registered check failed as worded); the merged wellington1922 decryption reproduced for all 60 runs (added check).

Runs divided into words, every departure marked; scripts/count_words.py: DCXXI.6.576.1 411 clean of an estimated 516 word places (0.797; on 27 Nov 2026 TOPETE was counted clean, 412, and then CASTILLO at L2.036 a hole, 411, because its Ñ bars are doubtful), DCXXI.8.731.1 76 of 86 (0.884).

After decoding: period pencil glosses over runs of DCXXI.6.576.1 pages 1-2 and its handwritten slip, and the CEHM catalogue records 91616 and 91927, compared; most glosses fit, three diverge (NOTES.md).
POST HOC, not counted: restarts or continuations of the key cycle read the address run of DCXXI.6.576.1 (fits the handwritten slip) and the repeated SEÑPR group as SEÑOR CORONA.

The clear text of both letters transcribed in full from the images by two AI helpers and the runs placed in it (reading_*.md), with an English translation keeping the holes (translation_*.md); the counted words unchanged. The 6.576.1 date line ('Agosto 25 de 1922') is on page 1.

All scripts rerun twice in the repository worktree (decrypt, count_words, test313, control_c1, control_c1b against ../, diagnostics): identical output both times and identical to the recorded files; decryption hashes unchanged.

validation.notes: Registered test (PLAN.md, frozen before decoding): key 313 passed on DCXXI.6.576.1 and DCXXI.8.731.1 (rank 1 of 19,683 shift triples, word coverage 0.708 and 0.645 against control maxima 0.075 and 0.118) and missed on DCXXI.5.442.1, 6.624.1, 7.647.1 and 7.657.2 (not read here; the misses do not rule the key out for them). Decoder check C1 failed as worded on cycle slips; C1b (added) reproduces all 60 runs of ../ (wellington1922).

texts.label: 'M. Cortés' to 'José González', 25 Aug 1922: 160 cipher runs
texts.summary: A felicista organiser in Puebla reports to Félix Díaz: intercepted correspondence; the local junta constituted in April; General Palma's movement near Tuxtepec; a meeting at Villa Guadalupe with Cástulo Pérez on the campaign in Veracruz and the Isthmus; Barrios proposed as chief of operations Tlaxcala-Puebla; commissions issued by the junta; the court-martial of Lazcano and Salgado; Gamboa informing on felicistas; five million pesos needed; his new signature 'J. J. Wellington' and a new address in Puebla. Signed M. Cortés.
texts.note: 411 clean words of an estimated 516 word places (0.797); 490 places (0.839) if each unread stretch counts as one word. Holes: one-letter slips, a repeated group read SEÑPR, unattested names, seven doubtful signs, seven stretches with no words.

texts.label: 'J. [?J.] Wellington' to 'José González', [Puebla], 1922: 14 cipher runs
texts.summary: The leaders of the coming rising in each part of Puebla state: Tomás Huerta (Tehuacán and neighbouring districts), José López Guillemín (Puebla-Tlaxcala border), Román Jiménez (Chiautla to Cholula), Ysabel Guerrero (the volcanoes), Márquez Galindo, Machorro and Bonilla (the Sierra), all awaiting the junta's last instructions.
texts.note: 76 clean words of 86 word places (0.884). Holes: one-letter slips in place names and in Machorro, one unidentified word.

gaps.detail: Slips or restarts of the key cycle; post hoc readings for .006 and .145, no frozen test.
Reads only with a restart of the cycle (post hoc SEÑOR CORONA).

gaps.item: Unattested names (MOLLANO, MOROPEZA, OLOARTE, TERRER, MAMEL, YNURRETA, YNTRRETA, GMMYOR)
gaps.detail: One occurrence each, no clear-text witness.

outcome.notes: Addition to targets/wellington1922 (one key per target: key 313 with the cycle running through each run). The parent's files are not changed. Andrew Beling decided on 25 Nov 2026 that the CEHM-Carso images may be used with AI readers; no image is committed.
